newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares trim losses, end almost unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares trim losses, end almost unchanged.

text.p: Philippine shares ended almost unchanged on Friday as investors remained cautious awaiting a cut in interest rates and first half company results, traders said.
The main index closed 0.11 points lower at 2,572.69 points, paring down an 18-point loss in midsession.
"With this currency market, people are looking for direction, foreign investors are basically sideways," said Carl Valentin, analyst at Asia Pacific Capital Equities.
Traders said gains in late session in San Miguel Corp B and a slight recovery in blue chips that fell sharply such as Meralco B and Petron Corp cut the market's losses.
"It's still a question of when the central bank will lower rates and until they do, this will overshadow corporate earnings," said Allan Araullo, vice-president at Regina Capital Development.
There were slightly more gainers versus losers at 64 to 56, while 53 remained unchanged.
Turnover was heavier at 2.1 billion pesos from the previous day's 1.63 billion.

"The trend next week will still be downwards. If the attack on the Southeast Asian currencies continues, we may be in for another correction," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital.
Week-on-week, the market shed 100.26 points, or 3.75 percent, from the previous Friday's 2,672.95 level.
Anscor-Hagedorn Securities said investors should remain liquid and take advantage of any rebound in the market.
Cecilio Castro, analyst at Anscor-Hagedorn advised: "Don't get yourself wet. Stay dry! Let these horrible times blow over first before seriously doing some investing again,"
